info.name: Mess_Tally
info.description:
Postman collection for the MessTally backend. Covers every route currently mounted in the app: `/api/v1/auth`, `/api/v1/mess`, and the root health route.

Base URL is controlled by the `baseUrl` collection variable (default: http://localhost:8000, matching PORT in .env). Login, Verify Email, Refresh Token, and Create Mess save the returned tokens into collection variables and also set the httpOnly cookies. Join Mess stores the joined mess and membership ids in collection variables.

Resend OTP re-issues a registration or password-reset code. It only works when that flow is already pending, and is limited to one request every 60 seconds with at most 3 resends per session.

Protected routes accept the access token either from the cookie jar or via the `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` header. `Refresh Token` reads the `refreshToken` httpOnly cookie, so it must run after Login, Verify Email, or Create Mess in the same Postman session.

request.description:
Validates the email with Zod, including a DNS MX lookup (domains that cannot receive mail, such as `gmail.co` or `example.com`, are rejected), stores the pending registration in Redis and emails a 6-digit OTP (valid for 5 minutes). The pending registration itself is kept for 1 hour so a new code can be requested after the OTP expires. The user is only created after Verify Email.

The sample body uses a real Gmail address because `example.com` publishes a null MX record and would be rejected.

A 60-second cooldown is enforced per email, so an immediate second Register call returns `429`.

Returns OTP timing metadata in `data`: `expiresInSeconds` (300), `resendAvailableInSeconds` (60) and `resendsRemaining` (3).

In development the OTP is also printed in the server console as `[dev] OTP <email> : <otp>`.

Validates the registration OTP, creates the user, sends the welcome email, and sets `accessToken` and `refreshToken` httpOnly cookies.

If the code has expired the API returns `Verification code has expired. Please request a new one.` — call Resend OTP with `purpose: "REGISTRATION"` to get a fresh code, since the pending registration survives for 1 hour. After 5 wrong codes the OTP is invalidated and the response is `429`.

The test script stores both tokens in collection variables.

Re-issues a 6-digit OTP when the previous one expired. `purpose` must be `REGISTRATION` (after Register) or `FORGOT_PASSWORD` (after Forgot Password).

The route only works when that flow is already pending. Without the Redis session created by Register or Forgot Password it returns `400` and sends nothing, so it cannot be called randomly.

Limits per email + purpose:
- `429` while the 60-second cooldown is still running; the message includes the seconds left.
- `429` after 3 resends in the same session; restart the flow with Register or Forgot Password.

The previous code is invalidated immediately. Response `data` contains `expiresInSeconds` (300), `resendAvailableInSeconds` (60) and `resendsRemaining`.

Other errors: `409` if the registration email is already registered, `403` if the account is suspended, deleted or unverified, and `404` if the user no longer exists.

Logs in an active, email-verified user and sets `accessToken` and `refreshToken` httpOnly cookies.

The test script stores both tokens in collection variables.

Returns the logged-in user's account and profile.

Requires a valid access token, supplied either by the `accessToken` cookie set during Login / Verify Email or by the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. The route is protected by `auth(Role.USER, Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPERADMIN)`.

Issues a new access token and refresh token using the `refreshToken` httpOnly cookie.

No request body is required, and the controller does not read an Authorization header — run Login, Verify Email, or Create Mess first so Postman has the refresh cookie. The test script updates both collection variables with the new tokens.

Sends a 6-digit password reset OTP to the email (valid for 5 minutes). The OTP is stored in Redis under `user-forgetPassword-otp:<email>`, and a 1-hour `user-forgetPassword-session:<email>` marker records that a reset is pending so the code can be re-sent later.

Only active, email-verified, non-deleted users can request a reset. A 60-second cooldown is enforced, so an immediate repeat call returns `429`. In development the OTP is printed in the server console.

Returns `expiresInSeconds` (300), `resendAvailableInSeconds` (60) and `resendsRemaining` (3) in `data`.

If the code expires, call Resend OTP with `purpose: "FORGOT_PASSWORD"`, then use the received OTP with Reset Password.

Verifies the password reset OTP sent by Forgot Password and updates the user's password.

The OTP must match `user-forgetPassword-otp:<email>` in Redis and expires after 5 minutes; once expired the API returns `Password reset code has expired. Please request a new one.` After 5 wrong codes the OTP is invalidated and the response is `429`.

A successful reset clears the pending session marker and the resend limits, so a later Forgot Password request starts with 3 fresh resends. A password-reset confirmation email is sent to the user after the password is updated.

Updates the authenticated user's profile information.

At least one of `bio`, `phone`, or `address` is required. All fields are optional and support empty strings for clearing existing values. Requires a valid access token and an active, email-verified account.

The route is protected by `auth(Role.USER, Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPERADMIN)`.

Uploads or replaces the authenticated user's profile image.

Send the image as `multipart/form-data` using the `profileImage` field. Only JPEG, PNG, and WebP images are accepted, with a maximum size of 5 MB. The previous Cloudinary image is deleted after a successful replacement.

**Before sending, select an actual image file in the `profileImage` field.** If that field is left empty, Postman fails locally with `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read` and the request never reaches the server. The request method must be `PATCH`.

Requires a valid access token and an active, email-verified account. The route is protected by `auth(Role.USER, Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPERADMIN)`.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Sunrise Mess",
  "address": "House 12, Road 3, Dhanmondi, Dhaka",
  "currency": "BDT",
  "mealCutoffTime": "11:00",
  "isJoinable": true,
  "requireApproval": true
}

request.description:
Creates a mess and makes the logged-in user its OWNER (also flagged as manager and ACTIVE). Protected by `auth()`, so any authenticated user can call it.

Only `name` is required; `address`, `currency`, `mealCutoffTime`, `isJoinable`, and `requireApproval` are optional. Server defaults: `currency` = "BDT", `mealCutoffTime` = "11:00", `isJoinable` = true, `requireApproval` = true.

A user can only be ACTIVE in one mess: if the caller already has an ACTIVE membership, this returns `409 Conflict` and asks them to leave that mess first.

The server pulls the next integer from the `mess_room_code_seq` PostgreSQL sequence and encodes it with Sqids, prefixed by the first three letters of the mess name (e.g. "Sunrise Mess" -> `SUN-JEVTDKRA`). It responds with `201` and `{ mess, accessToken, refreshToken }`. The new tokens include `messId`, and the test script stores `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `messId`, `roomCode`, and `messName` in collection variables.

Note: this route has no Zod validation yet, so invalid types are only caught by the service/Prisma.

Joins an existing mess using its `roomCode` (case-insensitive, trimmed). Protected by `auth()`, with `validateRequest` enforcing that `roomCode` is present.

Responds `201` with `{ mess, membership }`. The membership is `PENDING` when the mess has `requireApproval = true`, otherwise `ACTIVE`. Errors: `404` unknown room code, `403` when `isJoinable = false`, `409` when the user already has a `PENDING`/`ACTIVE` membership in this mess or is `ACTIVE` in another mess. A previous `LEFT` or `REJECTED` row is reused and reset to `MEMBER` with manager rights cleared.

Run Create Mess first to populate `roomCode`, but use an account that is not ACTIVE in another mess: creating and joining with the same user returns `409`. The test script stores `joinedMessId`, `membershipId`, and `membershipStatus`.
Basic health/welcome route. Returns `{ success: true, message: "Welcome to MessTally" }`.
